stem: The same auditor also wants continuous proof, not just a point-in-time statement, that every S3 bucket holding cardholder data stays encrypted going forward, and that none of those objects can be deleted before the mandated three-year retention period ends. Which TWO controls satisfy this? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: An AWS Config rule that evaluates each bucket's default encryption setting on an ongoing basis
A one-time AWS Artifact download of the current PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance
An S3 Lifecycle rule that expires the objects after three years
An IAM policy statement that denies s3:DeleteObject to every user
S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a three-year retention period on the affected objects

rationale: An AWS Config rule keeps checking the bucket's encryption setting on an ongoing basis, giving the continuous proof the auditor wants, and S3 Object Lock in compliance mode is the control that guarantees no principal can delete the affected objects before the three-year period ends. AWS Artifact's compliance documents describe AWS's own controls at a point in time; they say nothing about whether this startup's specific buckets stay encrypted or protected going forward. A Lifecycle expiration rule deletes objects once three years pass, but it does nothing to stop someone from deleting them early. An IAM policy that denies deletes to every user can be edited or overridden by anyone with permission to change IAM policies, so it does not give the same guaranteed immutability as Object Lock.
